claim: As of December 1, 2025 the Lingyin-Feilai Peak Scenic Area is free to enter (was RMB 45), open 7:30-17:30 with last entry 17:00, but Lingyin Temple itself still costs RMB 30; real-name online reservation required at least one day ahead.
quote: As of December 1, 2025, the Lingyin-Feilai Peak Scenic Area implemented a free-entry policy, with the site open daily from 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. (last entry at 5:00 p.m.). However, visitors entering Lingyin Temple itself must still purchase a temple admission ticket priced at RMB 30.

claim: Most visitors spend 2-3 hours exploring Lingyin Temple and the Feilai Feng grottoes; a fuller visit adding nearby temples and hiking can fill a half to full day.
quote: Most visitors spend 2-3 hours exploring the main temple complex and Feilai Feng. For a more leisurely visit, the recommended visit duration is half a day to one day.

claim: Leifeng Pagoda admission is 40 RMB (20 RMB half-price for students and visitors 70+); hours are seasonal: 8:00-17:30 in winter, 8:00-19:00 in spring, 8:00-20:00 May-October; equipped with elevators/escalators.
quote: The ticket price is 40 CNY... From November 1st to March 15th: 8:00-17:30... From March 16 to April 30: 8:00-19:00... May 1st - October 31st: 8:00-20:00... The pagoda also has elevators and escalators available for upper floors.

claim: Six Harmonies (Liuhe) Pagoda costs CNY 20 to enter plus CNY 10 to climb the pagoda; open roughly 7:00-17:30 (Apr-Oct) / 7:00-16:55 (Nov-Mar); a visit needs about 1-2 hours.
quote: Entrance fee is CNY20, with CNY10 for ascending the pagoda... 7:00 to 17:30 (April - October); 7:00 to 16:55 (November - March)... The recommended visiting hours is about 1 to 2 hours.

claim: The Liangzhu Ancient City Ruins Park (UNESCO World Heritage 2019) is open 09:00-17:00 (last entry 16:00), closed Mondays except holidays, with full-price admission around 60-80 RMB and a 20 RMB/person sightseeing shuttle for the large site.
quote: The park is generally open from 09:00 to 17:00 (last entry at 16:00). It is closed on Mondays... full price is around 60 RMB... A sightseeing shuttle ticket costs around 20 RMB/person... listed as a World Cultural Heritage Site by UNESCO in 2019.

claim: Plan 3-4 hours at the Liangzhu ruins park; it sits about a 40-minute drive from downtown (Metro Line 2 to Liangzhu Station plus shuttle/bus 1222M), and the in-park sightseeing shuttle (20 RMB) is recommended because the site is very large; real-name reservation needed.
quote: It's recommended to set aside 3 to 4 hours for your visit... take Hangzhou Metro Line 2 to Liangzhu Station, exit from Exit D, and then transfer to the shuttle bus or bus (route 1222M)... taking the sightseeing shuttle (20 RMB/person) is recommended.

claim: Hefang Street / Qinghefang is a free, roughly 1,800-meter pedestrian street open 24h (most shops 10:00-22:00) known for traditional Chinese medicine halls (Hu Qing Yu Tang), local snacks, silk, and the former residence of Hu Xueyan; best visited before 10am or after 7pm.
quote: The street is open 24 hours, with most shops open from 10:00 to 22:00... Hefang Street is free entry... stretching approximately 1,800 meters... Hu Qing Yu Tang, Yezhongde Tang, Baohe Tang... the Former Residence of Hu Xueyan.

claim: The China National Tea Museum is free with no ticket required, open 9:00-17:00 (May 1-Oct 7) / 8:30-16:30 (Oct 8-Apr 30), closed Mondays; set among Longjing tea plantations and gardens southwest of West Lake.
quote: Entry to the China National Tea Museum and its grounds is completely free, with no tickets required... May 1 - October 7: 9:00-17:00; October 8 - April 30: 8:30-16:30, and the museum is closed on Mondays... located in Shuangfeng Village by Longjing Road.
